instances.label_description: Diagnostic labels are the result of a clinical assessment of the participant. At each site a local clinician provided the diagnosis based on a clinical interview and appropriate work-up; for the psychiatric disorders cohort the assessment was determined from the participant's electronic health record or an active prescription, made outside data collection by an appropriately licensed clinician.

missing: Responses to optional questionnaire items and to cohort-specific instruments
why_missing: Some questions are optional, and each individual answered a common set of questions and then responded to additional questions relevant to their primary diagnostic category.
There may be data collection irregularities that caused some information to be missing from individual instances.

instances.instance_type: audio recording, represented by its derived features
instances.notes: Per-feature record counts in the version 3.1.0 release are: torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and sparc pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc EMA 28,640. Counts differ between features because representations derived from sensitive records and audio checks were withheld, and because some files could not generate certain features. The release does not state a single recording total and none is computed here.

known_biases.bias_description: Participants were recruited at a small number of high volume expert clinics; groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or who are less proximal to the collection sites, would have been less likely to be recruited.
known_biases.mitigation_strategy: The project states an intention to shift toward remote collection and to design recruitment so that more variables are controlled.

known_biases.bias_description: The dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors, and the public releases do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories.
known_biases.mitigation_strategy: Users should consider the multivariate distribution when assessing utility for different questions.

known_biases.bias_description: Participants were screened for different disorders based on site, so participants with different labels also had their data collected on different devices, confounding label with recording apparatus and site.
affected_subsets: All disease cohorts, since cohorts were recruited at different sites with distinct iPad devices.

sampling_strategies.strategies: Non-probability sampling. Recruitment of participants at high volume expert clinics within participating academic institutions, screened against per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria before the clinic visit.
sampling_strategies.source_data: Patients presenting at specialty clinics and institutions in five predetermined cohort groups, plus participants without the conditions of interest serving as controls.
sampling_strategies.why_not_representative: The dataset is a sample of a larger, ongoing collection and is not representative because it was collected at a limited number of geographic locations.
representative_verification: No verification of representativeness is reported; the project states an intention to make the sample more representative by shifting to remote collection and by designing recruitment to control for more variables.

subpopulations.identification: Age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status are recorded, and participants are assigned to disease cohort categories — voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders — or to the control group.
subpopulations.distribution: The public data releases do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories, and the dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors.
